title: Order Approving Petitions for Temporary Change Involving Transfer and Instream Flow Dedication of 25,000 Acre-Feet of Water (Walker River Irrigation District, Applications 2221 and 1389, Licenses 6000 and 9407)
authors: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Water Rights
publisher: California State Water Resources Control Board
finding: "The protocols establish accounting procedures for the conveyance of NFWF's Restoration Program water from Wabuska Gage through the Tribe's Reservation to Walker Lake"; the grant also funds "modernization of the Colony Ditch, Gage Peterson Ditch, and the Bridgeport Gatehouse which are currently un-modernized gage and measurement sites; and 2) continuation of a conveyance loss study."
conversion: none possible - document describes shepherding/measurement mechanism and an ongoing conveyance loss study but publishes no delivered-vs-released share
strengthWhy: Direct documentation of the shepherding mechanism the model assumes (legal instream dedication plus gage-based accounting protocols from upstream release to a terminal lake), by the agency that ordered it; but it quantifies no delivery fraction
differencesFromUtah: California/Nevada federal-decree adjudication rather than Utah state appropriation law; much smaller basin than the Great Salt Lake watershed; releases are reservoir stored water, not depletion-reducing conservation
verification: pdftotext of the fetched PDF, grep for 'conveyance', 'acre-feet', 'shepherd'

title: Order Approving Petitions for Temporary Change Involving Transfer and Instream Flow Dedication of 25,000 Acre-Feet of Water (Walker River Irrigation District)

title: Great Salt Lake Watershed Enhancement Trust Impact Report 2025
authors: Great Salt Lake Watershed Enhancement Trust (National Audubon Society / The Nature Conservancy)
finding: "Great Salt Lake Water Transactions (AF Diversion Basis)... 2023 ~64,000 af, 2024 ~69,190 af, 2025 ~72,485 af. *Includes a transaction of 7,213 af that was approved in 2023 but could not be delivered during season"
location: Water Transactions page, chart and footnote (txt lines 185-244)
conversion: The only explicit delivery failure disclosed is 7,213 af of 72,485 af transacted that 'could not be delivered during season', i.e. ~10% of the transacted volume did not reach the lake, implying a delivered share of about 0.90. This is a floor-level estimate: the Trust reports ALL volumes on a diversion basis and publishes no measured arrival volumes, so true delivery is likely lower.
strengthWhy: Exactly the mechanism and place the model is about - water dedicated upstream to Great Salt Lake, reported by the body doing it - but the report deliberately accounts on a diversion basis and gives no measured arrival volume, so 0.90 is inferred from one disclosed shortfall rather than measured
differencesFromUtah: None - this is Utah and Great Salt Lake itself. The limitation is accounting basis, not place.
verification: curl download (17 MB, under limit), pdftotext, grep for 'acre-feet|delivered|diversion basis'

title: Using Less of the Colorado River Takes a Willing Farmer and $45 Million in Federal Funds
authors: Alex Hager (KUNC), republished by Inside Climate News
place: Colorado River Upper Basin (Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico)
finding: "water being left in streams by SCPP-participating irrigators is not tracked to Lake Powell"; "officials are not measuring how much of that conserved water ends up in Lake Powell"; water rights laws "allow downstream users to simply take the water that an upstream user participating in the SCPP leaves in the river."
conversion: none possible - this is the strongest available evidence that the delivered share of dedicated water in the interior West is UNMEASURED, and that absent shepherding protection the share can in principle be driven toward zero by downstream re-diversion
strengthWhy: Same mechanism and region (paid upstream conservation intended to reach a downstream water body, in prior-appropriation states including Utah) and it directly addresses the model's two loss channels - conveyance tracking and re-diversion - but it reports an accounting gap, not a measured fraction
differencesFromUtah: Colorado River compact/interstate setting and a reservoir rather than a terminal lake; includes Utah among the four states, so water law is closely comparable
verification: WebFetch of the article; quotes returned verbatim

title: Searched for a measured delivered-share figure for dedicated/shepherded water reaching a terminal lake
finding: No source opened in this session publishes a measured ratio of water arriving at a terminal lake to water formally dedicated upstream. The Walker River order reports releases only; the Great Salt Lake Trust reports on a 'diversion basis'; the Colorado SCPP is explicitly 'not tracked to Lake Powell'.
strengthWhy: Searched Utah Division of Water Rights GSLDMP, GSL Watershed Enhancement Trust impact report, California State Water Board Walker River transfer orders, Colorado River System Conservation Pilot Program coverage, and peer-reviewed literature on instream-transfer conveyance loss. The 0.85 delivery_base is not supported by any published measurement found; the closest inference is ~0.90 from one disclosed non-delivery in the GSL Trust's own portfolio.
verification: web searches plus the four sources opened above; recorded as a genuine gap per spec

title: Weber Basin study: Secondary water meters drive down consumption
authors: Tim Vandenack (reporting Weber Basin Water Conservancy District study)
finding: The Weber Basin study of metered usage in the 2021 season "concluded that the presence of meters reduced consumption by 20% to 29%"; only the West Bountiful-Woods Cross area "provided reliable and consistent data" and the other four demand management areas "were left out of the study."
conversion: Midpoint of the reported 20-29% reduction in metered secondary water consumption, expressed as a share of prior use. This is a reduction in USE, not an increase in the delivered share of dedicated water, so it bounds the gross saving a metering programme can mobilise rather than measurement_gain_max directly.
strengthWhy: Utah, the exact HB 242 secondary-metering mechanism, measured on real consumption data - but it measures demand reduction, not improved delivery of dedicated water, and only one of five study areas had usable data
differencesFromUtah: none in place; the mechanism differs from the model's measurement_gain_max, which concerns arrival accounting rather than municipal demand
verification: WebFetch of the article; quotes returned verbatim and cross-checked against two independent search summaries

title: Man vs. Machine: Technological Promise and Political Limits of Automated Regulation Enforcement (Fresno automated water enforcement RCT)
authors: University of Chicago Energy & Environment Lab
publisher: Energy & Environment Lab, University of Chicago (EPIC)
finding: "automated enforcement decreases water use by 3 percent and violations by 17 percent"; the randomized controlled trial covered "over 80,000 households" in the City of Fresno, CA.
location: project page summary; working paper dated Nov 30, 2022
conversion: The RCT's treatment effect on water use is a 3% reduction; the compliance effect is a 17% reduction in violations. Used as the best randomized estimate of what metering-plus-telemetry enforcement does to use and compliance.
strengthWhy: Randomized, large, and directly about smart-meter telemetry driving compliance - the cleanest causal number available - but urban municipal enforcement in California, not agricultural shepherding of dedicated water in Utah
differencesFromUtah: urban households rather than irrigation; enforcement of hourly watering rules rather than protection of instream dedications; working paper, publication status unconfirmed
verification: WebFetch of the E&E Lab project page; quote returned verbatim
